newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares open mixed, seen quiet.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares open mixed, seen quiet.

text.p: Leading Russian shares were mixed in early trade on Tuesday and traders said they expected no drastic changes in market levels over the course of the day.
"In the absence of any important Russian news I think we can expect it either to fall or consolidate today," said Anton Kudryashov, head equity trader at Renaissance Capital.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index fell to 295.21 on Tuesday after closing on Monday at 295.61.
National power company UES EESR.RTS fell to $0.2120 at 0840 GMT from $0.2162 at Monday's close and regional power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS edged down to $1.253 from $1.255.

Kudryashov said U.S. investors were concentrating on the Dow Jones, which fell 43 points on Monday, despite periodic orders for second-tier shares, and he saw the market slackening as Russian national holidays in early May approached.
One dealer said the market could rise towards the end of the week, with some leading shares turning around as soon as today.
"Prices are going down for now but not for long," said Rinaco-Plus head trader Andrei Kukk. "Many securities will reach their minimum prices and turn up today."
But others said demand was not strong enough to turn the market around.

"There's not enough money for the market to grow," said Igor Kozhechkin, head trader at Rye, Man and Gor Securities. "There will be the ordinary ups and downs and by evening things will return to morning levels."
